method: Easter is the Sunday after the ecclesiastical full moon that falls on or after 21 March, so it is fixed by arithmetic on the year alone. The Western churches use the Gregorian calendar and the anonymous Gregorian computus, which reduces the month and day through the epact and the Sunday letter to month = floor(n / 31) and day = (n mod 31) + 1 with n = h + l - 7m + 114. The Orthodox churches keep the Julian calendar for the paschal full moon, so the Meeus Julian computus gives a Julian calendar date which is then converted to the civil calendar by adding the offset floor(year / 100) - floor(year / 400) - 2 days, the number of days the Julian calendar trails the Gregorian one in that year. The result is the Gregorian date of Orthodox Easter, and the difference between the two Easters is always a whole number of weeks because both fall on a Sunday. The nine moveable feasts are fixed offsets from Western Easter: Ash Wednesday -46 days, Palm Sunday -7, Maundy Thursday -3, Good Friday -2, Easter Monday +1, Ascension Day +39, Pentecost +49, Trinity Sunday +56 and Corpus Christi +60. The supported range is 1583, the first year after the Gregorian reform of 1582, to 4099, which keeps the offset formula and the four-digit input inside their valid span. All date arithmetic uses UTC midnight so a local timezone cannot shift a date, and the weekday is read from that UTC date. Input must be a plain four-digit year; empty fields, decimals, signs, five-digit years and years outside 1583 to 4099 are refused with the reason. Everything is calculated in the browser; nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.
